Concave down: $f''(x)<0$

$$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=6x^2+2x\\ f''(x)&=12x+2\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}12x+2&<0\\ 12x&<-2\\ x&<-\dfrac{1}{6}\end{aligned}$$

$f(x)$ is a parabola with vertex at the origin, so $f(g(x))$ behaves like $\big(g(x)\big)^2\ge 0$: the graph never goes below the $x$-axis and touches it where $g(x)=0$ (at the origin).

As $x\to 0^+$, $g(x)\to\infty$, so $f(g(x))\to\infty$; as $x\to\pm\infty$, $g(x)$ approaches a small positive constant, so $f(g(x))$ levels off above the axis.

Total marks lost $=25\bar{y}$

$$25\bar{x}+230=25\bar{y}\quad(1)$$

Sub $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$: $$\bar{y}=1.5\bar{x}+6\quad(2)$$

Sub (2) into (1):

$$\begin{aligned}25\bar{x}+230&=25(1.5\bar{x}+6)\\ 25\bar{x}+230&=37.5\bar{x}+150\\ 80&=12.5\bar{x}\\ \bar{x}&=6.4\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\bar{y}&=1.5(6.4)+6\\ \bar{y}&=15.6\end{aligned}$$

Since test is out of 40, marks gained $=40-y$

$\therefore$ least squares regression line for marks gained on lessons lost:

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Marks gained}&=40-(1.5x+6)\\ &=40-6-1.5x\\ &=-1.5x+34\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=-3x^2+12\\ \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}&=-6x\end{aligned}$$

Stationary points at $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$

$$\begin{aligned}0&=-3x^2+12\\ 3x^2&=12\\ x^2&=4\\ x&=\pm2\end{aligned}$$

At $x=-2$: $$\begin{aligned}y&=-(-2)^3+12(-2)-7\\ &=-(-8)+(-24)-7\\ &=-23\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}-2&=\dfrac{x-4.532}{0.135}\\ x-4.532&=-0.27\\ x&=4.262\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
